Summarise package structure and lines of code

Source: R/pkg_summary.R
pkg_summary.Rd

Combine pkg_structure() and pkg_lines() into one table. Each package is resolved (and, for GitHub or CRAN, downloaded) only once, so this is the quickest way to get everything about a set of packages.

Usage

pkg_summary(
  path = ".",
  include_ignored = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE,
  cache = c("session", "persistent", "none")
)

Arguments

path

A character vector of packages. Each element is one of:

  • A local folder, such as "." or "~/code/mypkg". Use "local::path" to be explicit.

  • A GitHub repository, such as "r-lib/cli" or a github.com URL. Add @ref for a branch, tag or commit ("r-lib/cli@v3.6.0"). For a package in a subfolder, use the github:: prefix: "github::owner/repo/subdir".

  • A CRAN package, such as "desc". Add @version for an older release ("cran::desc@1.4.0"). Archived packages are supported.

Without a prefix, existing local folders take precedence, then "owner/repo" is treated as GitHub and a bare name as CRAN. A path that does not exist (e.g. "./mypkg") is an error, not a GitHub request.

With several packages, one that cannot be analysed (a typo, a failed download) does not stop the others: it is reported in a warning and returned as a row of NAs whose package is the specification as given (pkg_functions() leaves it out instead). A single package that fails, or all packages failing, is an error.

include_ignored

If TRUE, also analyse files matched by the package's .Rbuildignore. Version-control folders and R's built-in build exclusions are always skipped.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress progress messages.

cache

Where to keep downloaded GitHub and CRAN packages:

  • "session" (default): a temporary folder, removed when R closes.

  • "persistent": a user cache folder kept across R sessions. Only fixed versions are stored there: CRAN releases and GitHub refs that look like a commit SHA or a version tag ("owner/repo@v1.2.0"). Requests that can change over time (no ref, or a branch) always fetch the latest code and use the session cache instead.

  • "none": always download afresh.

Use pkg_cache_clear() to empty a cache.

Value

A pkginspectr_tbl with one row per package: package, version, then the columns of pkg_structure() followed by those of pkg_lines().

See also

pkg_plot() to visualise the result.

Examples

pkg_summary(pkginspectr_example())
#> Summarising examplepkg...
#> # pkginspectr: Package summary, 1 package
#> # A tibble:    1 × 20
#>   package    version num_files num_dirs num_r_files num_function_r_files
#>   <chr>      <chr>       <int>    <int>       <int>                <int>
#> 1 examplepkg 1.2.3           9        6           2                    1
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: num_non_function_r_files <int>, num_test_files <int>,
#> #   num_vignettes <int>, num_docs <int>, num_data_files <int>,
#> #   total_lines <int>, code_lines <int>, comment_lines <int>,
#> #   roxygen_lines <int>, blank_lines <int>, r_lines <int>, test_lines <int>,
#> #   other_lines <int>, function_lines <int>

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
pkg_summary(c("r-lib/cli", "desc")) |>
  pkg_plot(type = "metric")
}
